lessons.title: Democracy in school and in the classroom

lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Define democracy and its basic principles
Describe how class and school elections work
Explain majority rule and respect for minorities
Explain the role of student councils
reviewNotes: Teacher to adapt voting procedures to the school's own rules for student leadership; no real elections or parties are discussed.

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: **Democracy** means 'rule by the people'. Its key principles are **equality** of all citizens, **freedom** to speak and take part, **free and fair elections**, **majority rule** with **respect for minorities**, and the **rule of law**. We learn democracy first in small groups: class, school clubs and student councils.

blocks.caption: Steps of a class election
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing candidates, campaign, secret ballot and count.

blocks.title: A class election
blocks.md:
1. **Call for candidates**: pupils who want to be class prefect put forward their names.
2. **Campaign**: candidates explain their plans politely and fairly.
3. **Secret ballot**: each pupil votes once on a slip of paper.
4. **Count** in public with witnesses.
5. **Announce** the winner, who gets the most votes, and the loser accepts the result.

**Majority rule** means that the option with most votes wins. But a democracy must also **protect minorities**: the winners should listen to those who lost and not treat them unfairly. After an election all should work together. In a **student council** pupils elect representatives who bring pupils' ideas to the school authorities; the council helps with discipline, activities and community projects.

blocks.title: Good democratic habits
blocks.md: Listen to different opinions, speak in turn, disagree without insulting, accept the result of a fair vote, respect the rules, and take responsibility. Cheating in elections, buying votes, threatening voters or refusing to accept a fair result is **undemocratic**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Democracy is not only voting: it also needs freedom to speak and respect for others.
- A secret ballot protects voters: do not force anyone to say how they voted.
- The majority cannot decide to take away the rights of the minority.

blocks.title: Example 1: counting
blocks.statement: In a class of 40 pupils, candidate A gets 18 votes, B gets 14 and C gets 8. Who wins, and does the winner have more than half of the votes?
steps: Half of 40 is 20; 18 is less than 20, so A wins with a plurality, not a majority of all.
blocks.answer: A wins with the most votes (18), but not more than half.

blocks.title: Example 2: respect for the loser
blocks.statement: After the election, candidate B is upset. What should the winner do?
steps: The winner should be gracious and respectful.
Invite B to help in the class committee.
blocks.answer: Be respectful and involve B in the work.

lessons.title: Unity in diversity and bilingualism

objectives: Explain the meaning and benefits of national unity
Describe attitudes that harm unity and ways to promote it
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify: the number of languages ('more than two hundred' is an approximate figure), the status of English and French, and the role of Pidgin English in the syllabus; the tone must remain respectful and non-political.

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: Cameroon has a very **diverse** population: more than two hundred languages are spoken, and the people practise different religions and belong to many ethnic groups and cultures. There are many traditional foods, dances, dress styles and festivals. This diversity is a **richness** of the nation. **National unity** means that all citizens, in spite of differences, feel they belong to one country and work together for its progress.

blocks.caption: Differences and common ground
blocks.alt: Two columns showing diversity and unity.

blocks.title: Official languages
blocks.md: Cameroon has **two official languages**, **English** and **French**, which have equal status. **Bilingualism** is the ability to use two languages. It helps communication across regions, access to education and jobs, trade and relations with the world, and supports national unity. The government and schools promote bilingual education and the use of both languages.

blocks.title: Promoting unity
blocks.md: Learn about other regions and languages; take part in national events and school exchanges; respect and greet people from other regions; marry, trade and work across regions; avoid insulting jokes about other groups; support sports teams and symbols that bring Cameroonians together; and speak out peacefully against discrimination.

Attitudes that harm unity include **tribalism** (favouring one's own group unfairly), **discrimination**, **hate speech**, **stereotypes** (unfair general ideas about groups), rumours and violence. Many people in Cameroon also speak local languages, Pidgin English, or other languages in addition to English or French; these languages are part of the national heritage.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Diversity is not a cause of conflict by itself: conflict comes from injustice and intolerance.
- Respecting my language does not mean looking down on others.
- Do not repeat stereotypes about regions or ethnic groups; judge people by their actions.

blocks.title: Example 1: benefits of bilingualism
blocks.statement: Give two benefits of being able to speak both English and French in Cameroon.
steps: You can talk to more Cameroonians.
You have more opportunities for study and work.

blocks.title: Example 2: unity
blocks.statement: Give two actions that help to build unity at school.
steps: Take part in cultural days to share each other's foods and dances.
Reject insulting jokes about other groups.
blocks.answer: Welcome pupils from other regions; join cultural days.
